short: A daring winter maneuver that forced Denmark's rapid capitulation in the Second Northern War.
full:
In early 1658, King Charles X Gustav's army was stranded in Jutland during his campaign against Denmark-Norway. Exploiting an unusually severe winter during the Little Ice Age, Swedish forces undertook a highly risky crossing of the frozen Little Belt to Funen on 30 January. Following this success, they marched across the wider and more treacherous ice of the Great Belt, reaching Zealand by 8 February.

This unprecedented logistical feat caught the Danish defenders entirely unprepared. Appearing suddenly outside Copenhagen, the Swedish army bypassed all naval defenses, forcing King Frederick III into immediate submission. The resulting panic compelled Denmark to sign the devastating Treaty of Roskilde three weeks later, yielding massive swathes of territory and permanently reshaping the Scandinavian map.
